name: Inland (Micro Center)
summary: Private store brand of US electronics retailer Micro Center, with no separate corporate entity, website or social presence. Inland filament is produced by eSUN or Polymaker (project-owner verified), identifiable by the spool cutout: diamond = Polymaker, round = eSUN. The catalogue mirrors those OEMs' own lines at Micro Center's budget in-store pricing.

oem_relationships.notes: User-verified (research/verified-oem-relationships.md): round spool cutout indicates eSUN production. Community mapping (VORON Design forum, not manufacturer-confirmed) matches Inland HS-PLA+ to eSUN PLA+ and notes eSUN spools carry an internal cardboard reinforcing ring; the same thread places this eSUN production in Vietnam.

User-verified (research/verified-oem-relationships.md): diamond spool cutout indicates Polymaker production. Community mapping (VORON Design forum, not manufacturer-confirmed) matches Inland PLA Matte to Polymaker Panchroma Matte PLA and Inland Cosplay PLA to Polymaker CosPLA Type A, and notes Polymaker spools have a pill-shaped hole near the spindle.

product_lines.name: PLA+ / HS-PLA+
product_lines.notes: Community-identified as equivalent to eSUN PLA+

product_lines.name: PLA Matte
product_lines.notes: Community-identified as equivalent to Polymaker Panchroma Matte PLA

product_lines.name: Cosplay PLA
product_lines.notes: Community-identified as equivalent to Polymaker CosPLA Type A

additional_notes: Inland is a label, not a manufacturer, so manufacturing_countries reflects its OEMs: China for Polymaker-sourced lines and Vietnam for eSUN-sourced lines (the Vietnam detail is community-reported and not manufacturer-confirmed). There is no Inland website, documentation, wiki or social media; the Micro Center category page is the only endpoint. Micro Center stocks build plates and PEI sheets in store but they are Creality-branded, so makes_plates is false. In-store filament typically runs $17-20/kg. Community quality complaints about Inland silk PLA appear on the Bambu Lab forum (anecdotal, unverified). Spools carry no manufacturer information, so consumer-facing sourcing is deliberately opaque.

provenance.conflicts: The verified-oem-relationships file names eSUN generically while the VORON forum thread places eSUN's Inland production in Vietnam specifically; this is treated as a refinement rather than a contradiction, but it is community-sourced and not manufacturer-confirmed. The same thread cautions that sourcing could change at any time and that all SKU-to-OEM mappings are indirect, so per-line OEM assignment should not be considered settled.
